correctness.rationale: Let q>=2 be an order for which an actual finite projective plane exists (no Desarguesian hypothesis). In its bipartite point-line incidence graph, radius-2 vertex neighborhoods are P∪L(p) and L∪P(ℓ). Hence scale-four Čech K=A∪B with both A and B cones and exact A∩B=J_P*J_L; the equality of mixed faces uses independent collinearity/concurrency conditions. Because each point pair lies on a unique line, collapse each line simplex to a star tree independently: J_P and its dual J_L each become a connected graph with v=q²+q+1 vertices, qv edges and cycle rank q³. Thus K≃Σ(J_P*J_L)≃∨^{q⁶}S⁴ integrally. There are 2v maximal simplices of dimension (q+1)²; the same complex holds 4<=r<5, and all balls meet at an incidence-edge midpoint for r>=5. Independent q=2 enumeration gives 7,919 nonempty faces and exactly 64 reduced H₄ classes; q=3 incidence graph confirms 26 facets and q³=27 factor cycle ranks. Finite checks corroborate, not replace, all-order incidence-axiom proof.

evidence: The published Resultary Steiner-design theorem covers J_P and J_L independently (q³ circle ranks); published Heawood full Cech filtration covers q=2. Neither, as read, proves exact Cech scale-four suspension of their join uniformly for any projective plane. Published scale-two Vietoris–Rips projective plane theorem computes q³ S² but not this q⁶ S⁴ Čech construction.

value.rationale: A uniform exact fourth-homotopy class invariant q⁶ for every existing projective plane including non-Desarguesian examples is a natural incidence-geometry/topology theorem. Cone-join factorization makes the result conceptually reusable for incidence hypergraphs.
